beginner_en:
Rabbeinu now unpacks the **Gemara in Sanhedrin (99b)** that tells of **Rabba** who was sitting and saw a **nachash** (snake) trying to swallow a **frog** (uvra) — and then saw a **pushkantza** (which Rashbam explains is a **raven**) come and swallow the frog and thereby **protect it from the snake** — and then saw the raven **ascend and sit in a tree**. Rabba exclaimed: **'Ta chazi kama nafish cheilei d'ilana!'** — 'Come see how great is the strength of this tree!'

Rabbeinu reads this entire sugya as an allegory for the **Gemara-learning dynamic**:

**The nachash = the danger of Torah shelo lishmah**. **"Heyno al yedei she'yilmad shelo li'shmah yivla osah ha'nachash"** — 'i.e., when one learns not for the sake of Heaven, the nachash swallows it.' The Torah one has learned can be seized by the sitra achra when learned with ulterior motive.

**Rabba's statement specifies the danger**: **Rashbam explains "Rabba kamar lah"** — 'Rabba said it' — as meaning: **"heyno al yedei she'yilmod bishvil she'yikarei Rabbi"** — 'i.e., when one learns in order to be called Rabbi.' That specific shelo-lishmah — learning for the title — is what feeds the nachash.

**The raven = learning at night**: **"Asa pushkantza — u'feresh Rashbam: orev"** — 'the pushkantza came — Rashbam explains: a raven.' And the Rebbe now exegetes: **"heyno al yedei she'yilmad ba'lailah, mi'lshon arvis"** — 'i.e., through one learning at night, from the expression *arvis* (evening/maariv).' See Rashi to Eruvin 22a on the phrase "mashkim u'ma'ariv." The raven (orev) = the one who learns at night (ma'ariv).

**And the raven 'swallowing' the frog**: **"u'valah — heyno u'meigen alav min ha'nachash ha'nizkar l'eil"** — 'and swallowed — i.e., it shields him from the aforementioned nachash.' Night-learning protects one's Torah from the shelo-lishmah-swallowing danger.

**The tree = Avraham**: **"v'saliq y'siv b'ilana — peresh ha'Maharsha, she'hu bechinas Avraham, she'kasuv etzlo (Bereishis 21:33): 'va'yita eishel' she'hu bechinas chesed"** — 'and ascended and sat in the tree — the Maharsha explains this is the aspect of Avraham, regarding whom it is written "and he planted an *eishel*" — which is the aspect of chesed.' **"heyno she'ha'chut shel chesed she'nimshach alav meigen alav min ha'nachash ha'nal"** — 'i.e., the thread of chesed drawn upon him shields him from the aforementioned nachash.' Nighttime Torah draws down chut shel chesed (see Chagigah 12b) — which is the tree Avraham planted — and this chesed is the **second layer** of protection beyond the raven's swallowing.

**"Ta chazi kama nafish cheilei d'ilana"**: **"heyno she'Rabba masmiha es atzmo, she'kol kach gavar aleinu chasdo, she'afilu al zeh yachol l'hagen"** — 'i.e., Rabba is astonished at himself: His chesed has so overwhelmed us that it can even shield against this [spiritual danger of shelo-lishmah]!' The wonder of Hashem's chesed is not merely that it provides for physical needs, but that it protects Torah-learners from the cosmic nachash of ulterior motive.
intermediate_en:
Rabbeinu unpacks the Sanhedrin 99b sugya (Rabba seeing nachash→frog→pushkantza→tree):

**Nachash=Torah shelo li'shmah** that 'yivla osah ha'nachash.' Rashbam **"Rabba kamar lah"**=**"she'yilmod bishvil she'yikarei Rabbi"** — specific shelo-lishmah of title-seeking.

**Pushkantza=orev** (Rashbam)=**"she'yilmad ba'lailah, mi'lshon arvis"** (Rashi Eru 22a **mashkim u'ma'ariv**). **"U'valah=u'meigen alav min ha'nachash."**

**Saliq y'siv b'ilana** (Maharsha)=**Avraham**, bechinas **"va'yita eishel"** (Bereishis 21:33)=**chesed** — **chut shel chesed** meigen alav min ha'nachash.

**"Ta chazi kama nafish cheilei d'ilana"** — Rabba masmiha: **"she'kol kach gavar aleinu chasdo, she'afilu al zeh yachol l'hagen."**
intermediate_he:
רבינו מבאר סוגיית סנהדרין צט: (רבה ראה נחש→אוברא→פושקנצא→אילן):

**נחש=תורה שלא לשמה** ש"יבלע אותה הנחש." רש"ב"ם **"רבה קאמר לה"**=**"שילמוד בשביל שיקרא רבי"** — שלא-לשמה של רדיפת השם.

**פושקנצא=עורב** (רש"ב"ם)=**"שילמד בלילה, מלשון ערבית"** (רש"י עיר' כב. **משכים ומעריב**). **"ובלעה=ומגן עליו מן הנחש."**

**סליק יתיב באילנא** (מהרש"א)=**אברהם**, בחינת **"ויטע אשל"** (בר' כא, לג)=**חסד** — **חוט של חסד** מגן עליו מן הנחש.

**"תא חזי כמה נפיש חיליה דאילנא"** — רבה מתמיה: **"שכל כך גבר עלינו חסדו, שאפילו על זה יכול להגן."**
scholarly_he: סנ' צט: — נחש/אוברא/פושקנצא/אילנא. נחש=תשל"ל; רש"ב"ם רבה קאמר לה=בשביל שיקרא רבי. פושקנצא=עורב=ערבית (רש"י עיר' כב.); בלעה=הגנה. מהרש"א: אילן=אברהם=אשל=חסד (בר' כא, לג). כה"נ"ד=תמיהת רבה שאף שלל"ש חסד מגן.
